The autologous platelet-rich plasma (PRP) gel has been shown to have a positive effect on healing after surgical extraction of mandibular third molars. The study found that patients in the PRP group experienced reduced pain, swelling, and trismus compared to those in the control group. Additionally, the PRP group demonstrated enhanced and faster bone healing compared to the control group.

This suggests that using autologous PRP gel as a treatment for mandibular third molar surgery may be beneficial for promoting optimal healing and reducing complications.

It is essential to note that while PRP gel has shown promising results in this study, more research is needed to fully understand its effects on dental surgeries. However, based on the findings presented, autologous PRP gel appears to be a viable option for enhancing healing after surgical extraction of mandibular third molars.
